claims.text: HfZrTiTa0.53 should be cryogenically rolled near liquid-nitrogen temperature and then annealed at 400–500 °C for 5–15 minutes.
The initial HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy has a yield strength of approximately 786 MPa.
The initial HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy has a compressive strength of approximately 1314 MPa.
The initial HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy has a uniform tensile elongation of approximately 13.5%.
The conventional HfZrTiTa0.53 microstructure is coarse and this coarseness limits tensile ductility.
Cryogenic deformation suppresses recovery and thereby promotes a high density of deformation twins.
A short intermediate anneal will partially recover or recrystallize the rolled structure and refine subgrains while retaining most deformation twins.
Deformation twins act as strong barriers to mobile dislocations and can enhance yield strength.
Nanoscale twins and refined subgrains impede crack initiation and facilitate cooperative dislocation slip.
The increased twin density will improve strain hardening and delay tensile necking.
At room temperature and a quasi-static tensile strain rate below 10^-3 s^-1, the treated alloy will exceed 25% uniform tensile elongation.
An elongation above 25% would represent an improvement of more than 50% over the stated 13.5% baseline.
The treatment will preserve a yield strength near 786 MPa.
HfZrTiTa0.53 has proven high impact-triggered energy release in its baseline state.
The treatment will preserve the impact-triggered energy-release characteristics of HfZrTiTa0.53.
The proposed mechanism and benefits are applicable specifically to room-temperature quasi-static tension below 10^-3 s^-1, with corresponding compression and high-rate impact assessment.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome uses an absolute threshold of greater than 25% uniform elongation, whereas the falsification rule refers ambiguously to improvement 'beyond 25% relative to the baseline,' which could mean a 25% relative increase rather than 25% absolute elongation.

The predicted-outcome text says either no twin-density increase or no ductility improvement would falsify the hypothesis, but the formal rule requires both failures together before falsification, except when strength or impact energy deteriorates.
